source_notes: Documented money-laundering and fraud typologies drawn from public reporting exemplars (FATF, FATF-Generative-AI, Chainalysis, Europol, INTERPOL, ENISA, FBI IC3, UNODC, Verizon DBIR, SEC/OFAC advisories) and sanitised illustrative STR themes, mapped against the Drift Sentinel DS-01..DS-40 rulebook. For hackathon demonstration only - all fixtures are synthetic and illustrative; they contain no personal or confidential data.

typologies.name: Investment/Ponzi crypto fraud
typologies.source: FATF Virtual Assets Red Flags / Chainalysis Crypto Crime 2023-24
typologies.description: Victims are induced to deposit crypto into a fraudulent investment scheme promising high returns, often run via a cloned or fake trading platform with AI-generated marketing personas.
typologies.expected_gap: source of funds corroboration (DS-27)

typologies.name: Pig-butchering / romance scam (AI persona)
typologies.description: Criminals groom victims through social or dating channels using AI-generated personas and deepfake media, building trust before steering them into fake crypto investment platforms.
typologies.expected_gap: source-of-wealth inconsistency during relationship (DS-27)

typologies.name: Mule / money-mule pass-through network
typologies.description: Criminals recruit money mules who open crypto accounts or use their own wallets to receive and pass through illicit funds, often via fresh wallets created on demand.
typologies.expected_gap: mule-behaviour detection when no overt coaching markers (DS-40)

typologies.name: AI-cloned voice / phishing of account access
typologies.description: Fraudsters use AI-generated voice clones and realistic phishing pages mirroring the exchange app to obtain login credentials and wallet keys.
typologies.expected_gap: AI-orchestrated voice/credential takeover not yet a named rule (DS-06/DS-24 only partially catch)

typologies.name: Synthetic identity new-customer fraud
typologies.description: Fraud programmes assemble synthetic identities from aggregated real and fabricated data (including AI-generated documents) to pass KYC and onboard as new customers, then transact at scale before detection.
typologies.expected_gap: ongoing post-onboarding source-of-funds monitoring (DS-27/DS-29)

typologies.name: Stablecoin cross-border payment structuring
typologies.description: Stablecoin rails used for cross-border payments are structured to avoid travel-rule and transaction thresholds, exploiting gaps in originator information transmission.
typologies.expected_gap: travel-rule threshold structuring evade for non-covered rails (DS-34)

typologies.name: Romance scam with AI deepfake video persona
typologies.description: Scammers sustain long-running fake relationships through AI-generated video calls, producing near-real-time deepfake faces to defeat user-side verification, then route victim funds into fresh unhosted wallets.
typologies.expected_gap: counterparty due diligence on unhosted receivers (DS-04/DS-26)

typologies.name: Deepfake liveness-bypass document fraud
typologies.description: Fraudsters defeat KYC liveness checks with deepfake face-swap media and forged identity documents, onboarding under borrowed identities at speed before onboarding monitors desensitise.
typologies.expected_gap: incomplete-KYC enrolment accepted despite undetected liveness bypass (DS-07)

typologies.name: Account takeover via credential stuffing
typologies.description: Password lists harvested from breaches are replayed across exchange accounts. Stolen sessions are used for rapid withdrawals before the victim notices, with funds moving from a now-shared-credential profile.
typologies.expected_gap: CDD-only monitoring cannot tell shared-credential resets from routine change (DS-07/DS-27)

typologies.name: Corporate KYB 'door-opener' front company
typologies.description: A front company with credible-looking KYB documents onboard as a corporate client; the true economic controller uses nominee officers and refuses beneficial-ownership disclosure, then runs deposits through the account.
typologies.expected_gap: source-of-wealth verification for controlling shareholders (DS-27)

typologies.name: Shell-company nominee / DPO layering conduit
typologies.description: Legal-entity shells with designated persons (officers) accumulate funds from multiple operating companies, pass them through corporate accounts to third-party shell recipients, while beneficial ownership stays unverified.
typologies.expected_gap: pass-through corporate conduits evade counterparty due diligence (DS-04/DS-26)

typologies.name: Deposit-dispersion fan-out structuring
typologies.source: FATF 2020 Outcome-based Recommendations / classic structuring casework
typologies.description: Criminal proceeds are dispersed from a master account in sub-threshold round transfers to a small cluster of wallets, reassembled elsewhere - classic structuring recomposed for crypto rails.
typologies.expected_gap: structuring that carries an articulated rationale escapes anomaly reason checks (DS-38)

typologies.name: Peel-chain layering with token swaps
typologies.description: Funds are split and re-split across fresh wallets ('peeling'), converted through token swaps and privacy coins, so single-hop rules see only small, benign-looking transfers.
typologies.expected_gap: multi-hop peel chains evade fan-out consolidation detection (DS-05/DS-15)

typologies.name: Cross-chain bridge / chain-hopping obfuscation
typologies.description: Funds are moved across blockchains through native bridges and exchange-internal swaps, shattering a single-chain audit trail while sitting under each platform's per-chain monitoring.
typologies.expected_gap: cross-chain hop sequences are invisible to single-chain fan-in/out logic (DS-05/DS-15)

typologies.name: Mixer-assisted sanitisation
typologies.description: Proceeds pass through a mixing/tumbling service to break the on-chain link to criminal origin; the exchange only ever sees post-mix inputs with no traceable provenance.
typologies.expected_gap: post-mix inputs defeat link-analysis where sanitisation is not itself flagged (DS-15)

typologies.name: Privacy-coin conversion layer (Monero-style)
typologies.description: Funds are converted into privacy coins and back to transparent assets at unhosted wallets, exploiting concealment by design plus token-swap rails that most indicator libraries do not monitor natively.
typologies.expected_gap: conversion-layer concealment is treated as routine token activity (DS-15)

typologies.name: Ransomware payment facilitation
typologies.description: Ransom affiliates route victim payments through high-risk jurisdictions and threat-intelligence-flagged addresses; screening misses them because the receiving address is not yet on a published list.
typologies.expected_gap: first-seen ransom addresses evade sanctions/risk-list screening (DS-21)

typologies.name: Sextortion / financial-release extortion
typologies.source: UNODC Human Trafficking & ML 2023 / NC3 sextortion advisories
typologies.description: Victims are coerced into paying a 'release fee' via cryptocurrency; perpetrators use naive victim wallets and darknet-purpose memos, with a low-history beneficiary collecting the sums.
typologies.expected_gap: small-sum victim-to-perpetrator transfers avoid material transfer safeguards (DS-35)

typologies.name: Authorised push payment fraud via deepfake calls
typologies.source: Europol 2024 / UK PSR APP fraud review 2024
typologies.description: Fraudsters impersonate bank or exchange staff in AI-generated voice/video calls, coercing victims into transferring funds from their own accounts - transfers that are customer-authorised and therefore hard to detect.
typologies.expected_gap: customer-authorised outflows to deepfake-directed recipients miss anonymity checks (DS-24)

typologies.name: Pension / life-savings restructuring abuse
typologies.description: Victims are persuaded to 'restructure' retirement savings into small sub-threshold withdrawals and onward investments; velocity spikes on legacy accounts signal the abuse but comply with each individual threshold.
typologies.expected_gap: articulated-rationale velocity spikes evade no-rationale anomaly logic (DS-38)

typologies.name: ESports skin-gambling layering
typologies.source: FATF Virtual Asset Compliance 2021 / ESMA markets 2024
typologies.description: Crypto moved onto immersive-gaming platforms is churned through loot crates and skin trades, converted at unlicensed skin-exchanges, and withdrawn as fiat - opaque to conventional transaction monitoring.
typologies.expected_gap: skin-gaming churn is below structural detection without named-platform coverage (DS-05/DS-19)

typologies.name: Fake crypto exchange rug-pull
typologies.source: Chainalysis Crypto Crime 2024 / SEC enforcement actions 2024
typologies.description: Cloned-exchange platform oboards retail users, aggregates deposits through sub-threshold investment tickets, then freezes withdrawals and exits - with the platform never registered or screened.
typologies.expected_gap: unregistered-platform counterparties evade risk-list and rationale checks when activity is framed as investment (DS-31/DS-38)

typologies.name: Pump-and-dump token inflation
typologies.description: Coordinated clusters inflate a low-cap token with rapid successive high-value buys, then distribute to insiders - behavioural spikes on a single asset mirroring classic market-abuse wash patterns.
typologies.expected_gap: coordinated buy-spike suffers no pass-through check beyond velocity (DS-23)

typologies.name: NFT / lootbox wash-trading
typologies.description: Wash-trading between a controller's own wallet cluster gives artificial trading volume to shared-narrative NFTs, moving value via embedded royalties and 'sweep' mechanisms outside monitored asset classes.
typologies.expected_gap: collection wash-trading only partially caught by clustering rules (DS-23)

typologies.name: Fresh-wallet mule factory
typologies.description: A network of newly created wallets receives mule-driven deposits, obeys coached small-set instructions, and is drained through unhosted wallets - each wallet demonstrably low-history yet moving material sums.
typologies.expected_gap: fresh-wallet factory is caught per-wallet but not as a coordinated pass-through set (DS-23)

typologies.name: SIM-swap-driven account takeover
typologies.description: Attackers port the victim's mobile number, reset credentials, change device/IP fingerprints, and withdraw before anomaly detectors learn the new behavioural baseline.
typologies.expected_gap: credential-profile churn is not surfaced as shared-credential risk until after the fact (DS-06)

typologies.name: Unlicensed VASP jurisdiction hopping
typologies.source: FATF Recommendations 19/21 / EU AMLR licensing regimes 2024
typologies.description: Clients deliberately use unlicensed or unregulated VASPs in low-enforcement jurisdictions, relocating activity when a jurisdiction raises its controls - evading registration-based screening.
typologies.expected_gap: anonymisation on unlicensed platforms escapes technology-layer monitoring (DS-24)

typologies.name: Grey-list / high-risk corridor travel-rule gap
typologies.description: Transfers to enhanced-monitoring (grey-list) jurisdictions routinely arrive with incomplete originator information, exploiting travel-rule exemptions on smaller-value and cross-border corridors.
typologies.expected_gap: travel-rule exemptions for small cross-border corridors evade originator-information rules (DS-20/DS-34)

typologies.name: Sanctioned-entity wallet interop
typologies.description: A counterparty appears behind an unhosted wallet and unverified onboarding gaps; the address is not yet on published sanctions lists, so screening fails despite elevated jurisdiction risk.
typologies.expected_gap: first-seen sanctioned-adjacent wallet escapes matching until list publication (DS-21)

typologies.name: Darknet marketplace value transfer
typologies.source: UNODC 2023 World Drug Report / Chainalysis darknet studies
typologies.description: Marketplace proceeds paid with stolen cards and criminal-source crypto are withdrawn via memos referencing illicit goods, moving from darknet-tagged wallets to high-risk jurisdictions.
typologies.expected_gap: marketplace-to-exchange flows evade unregistered-platform detection when memos are sanitised (DS-19)

typologies.name: PEP nominee conduit
typologies.description: A politically exposed person routes funds through corporate conduits and designated nominee signatories; enhanced diligence is bypassed because the PEP is not a named account holder and UBO sources go unverified.
typologies.expected_gap: conduit-held PEP funds evade source-of-wealth checks in corporate wrappers (DS-27)

typologies.name: Unregistered P2P arbitrage cash-out
typologies.source: FATF Recommendation 16 implementation / national P2P advisories
typologies.description: Crypto is cashed out through peer-to-peer arbitrage on unregistered platforms, converting sub-threshold tranches to fiat via crypto-to-card rails - bypassing both exchange registration and round-trip detection.
typologies.expected_gap: P2P cash-out escapes no-rationale anomaly logic when framed as arbitrage (DS-38)

typologies.name: Fresh-wallet AI-coached mule victims
typologies.description: Victims are recruited through AI-generated video ads into 'work from home' schemes; they open fresh wallets, receive coached transfers, and forward funds, with limited financial literacy hiding the mule role.
typologies.expected_gap: AI-recruited low-literacy mules evade single-hop pass-through aggregation (DS-23)

typologies.name: LLM-generated bulk phishing / mass ATO
typologies.description: LLM tooling produces thousands of adaptive phishing pages and credential lures, leading to bulk account takeover across a clustered wallet population whose sessions share fingerprints.
typologies.expected_gap: mass ATO evades anonymous-traffic detection when sessions are proxied per user (DS-24)

typologies.name: Trust-transfer scam to cross-border funnel
typologies.source: FBI IC3 2024 / UK FCA fraud 2024 review
typologies.description: Victims in trust-transfer scams (grandparent, family-support, impersonation) remit to a cross-border funnel of naive, low-history wallets where originator details are stripped before the final hop.
typologies.expected_gap: cross-border trust-transfer funnel defeats unhosted-receiver due diligence at the retail layer (DS-26)
